=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## 1. Preliminary point: how the Seller has framed the package

The covering material says that items marked **[STANDARD]** have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides," are "FINAL," and need no scrutiny. It also says we have "already accepted" the disclosure framework and the limitation package. **I have not relied on any of that.** These are negotiating assertions in the counterparty's draft. Nothing in the documents evidences any principal-level agreement. Almost every [STANDARD] item is adverse to us, and several conflict with the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.

**Action:** Confirm internally whether Wattlebridge's principals agreed to any of these points. Unless they did, respond in writing that we do not accept the categorisation and that all positions remain open.

The "market context" preamble is also selective. A 10–20% cap and 12–18 month period can be within range for general warranties. It is not market to put title, capacity, tax, or specific indemnities under those limits. Combining buyer-knowledge exclusion with general data-room disclosure is a seller-favourable position, not a standard one.

## 2. Material issues

### A. The disclosure and knowledge regime (highest structural risk)

**1. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2, Schedule 7)**
- **Problem:** Every warranty is qualified by everything in DD-002 to DD-012, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Combined with the items below, the warranties become close to worthless.
- **Push back:**
  - Only matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter count, meaning disclosed with sufficient detail for a buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect.
  - No general disclosure of the data room. At most, accept specifically identified documents for specific warranties.
  - Disclosure must never qualify fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity, or specific indemnities.

**2. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)**
- **Problem:** This excludes claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, *or which was discoverable* from the data room or public records. It is an anti-sandbagging clause of the broadest kind. It would bar claims on every issue in this memo, because we identified them all from the data room.
- **Push back:** Delete it. Replace it with an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, except matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. Fallback: actual knowledge only, of named individuals, at signing.

**3. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, and the 12.3/13 "default" rule)**
- **Problem:** The proposed default is that every limitation applies to every claim unless expressly excluded. As drafted, it captures fraud, title, tax, indemnities and leakage.
- **Push back:**
  - Reverse the default. Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
  - Carve out fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its representatives.
  - Exclude from the limitations: fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity/deed, all specific indemnities, leakage and completion-accounts adjustments, and covenant breaches.
  - Note that non-reliance clauses will not reliably exclude statutory misleading-conduct claims (ACL s 18) in any event. We should not concede them as drafted.

### B. Fundamental, title and tax

**4. Title and capacity warranties capped and time-limited with general warranties**
- **Problem:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title fails, we lose the asset we paid AUD 24m for, and the Seller's position would cap our recovery at AUD 4.8m within 18 months.
- **Push back:**
  - Cap at 100% of price (AUD 24m).
  - Time limit of at least 6–7 years, or the statutory limitation period.
  - No de minimis or basket.
  - Not qualified by disclosure.

**5. Title evidence (DL 10, DD-012)**
- **Problem:** The Seller relies only on its own share register. The DL expressly notes we have not verified it.
- **Push back:**
  - Run our own ASIC company extract and historical search, and a PPSR search against Harbourglass and Paperbark.
  - Check whether Riverlark holds security over the shares or the company.
  - Obtain the original share certificates, signed transfer forms, and evidence of no options, convertibles or employee equity rights.
  - Make delivery of these items a Completion deliverable.

**6. Tax "settled under the general regime"**
- **Problem:** Tax exposure must not sit inside a 20% cap and 18-month window. ATO amendment periods are commonly 4 years or longer.
- **Push back:**
  - A separate tax indemnity or tax deed covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and superannuation guarantee shortfalls.
  - Cap at 100% of price.
  - Claims period of at least 5–7 years.
  - No basket, and not qualified by disclosure.

### C. General warranty limitations

**7. Cap (cl 12.1, 20% / AUD 4.8m)**
- This is within range for general warranties only. Consider whether W&I insurance is proposed. If it is, structure around it.
- **Illustration:** The debt-like items below (Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs, Sandbar AUD 330k) total about **AUD 3.95m**. That would consume roughly 82% of the cap if left as warranty claims. These items must sit in the price mechanics, not the warranty regime.

**8. Thresholds (cl 12.2)**
- **Problem:** The basket of AUD 250k (about 1.04%) is a **deductible**, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Push back:**
  - A **tipping** basket, so the full amount is recoverable once exceeded.
  - Lower the basket to about 0.5% (AUD 120k).
  - De minimis of about AUD 10k.
  - Related or same-cause claims must aggregate for the de minimis. This matters for the three Sandbar renewals and any data-incident claims.
  - Neither threshold applies to indemnities or tax.

**9. Time limit (cl 12.3, 18 months)**
- Push for 24 months, which covers two full audit cycles. Accept 18 months only as a trade.

### D. Specific transaction issues

**10. Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL 2; DD-002)**
- **Facts:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (around AUD 3.6m). The Seller says the consent is "addressed," but its own DL says no written consent has been obtained and the 11.3 conditions are not evidenced. "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation. Treating "delivery of the counterparty's written consent" as satisfying the condition ignores the 11.3 conditions.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a **Condition Precedent for the Buyer's benefit**, waivable only by the Buyer.
  - It is satisfied only by an unconditional written consent and waiver from Bluefen, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, plus evidence that all clause 11.3 conditions are met.
  - The Seller must use "all reasonable endeavours," and Bluefen terms may not be amended adversely to obtain consent.
  - Include a long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
  - Consider a specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates or materially reduces volumes within an agreed period after Completion.

**11. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL 3; DD-003), about AUD 3.2m**
- **Problem:** "Release following Completion" is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal. Change of control under cl 8.1 may itself trigger default or acceleration. We would close with security still registered.
- **Push back:**
  - Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price, under a **payout letter**. It must cover principal, interest, break costs and fees, and be treated as Financial Indebtedness deducted from price.
  - A deed of release and PPSR discharges (including any share security) delivered at Completion.
  - Any change-control waiver required before Completion.
  - A specific indemnity for any residual Riverlark liability.

**12. Completion bonuses (DD-005; DL 5), AUD 420,000 plus on-costs**
- **Problem:** The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller," yet they are a **Company liability** omitted from the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and PAYG are not addressed. Bonuses with continued-employment conditions may fall due after Completion, when the Company is ours.
- **Push back:**
  - Treat the full amount plus employer on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, workers' comp as applicable) as Transaction Costs or Debt deducted from price.
  - Payment through Company payroll at or immediately after Completion, funded from price, with PAYG withheld.
  - Itemise it in the funds flow.
  - Add a specific indemnity outside cap and basket.

**13. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004; DD-010; DL 4)**
- **Problem:** Title to the SOW3 Project Materials only passes on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is shown as open, with no receipt or assignment in the data room. The real risk is that the Company does not own IP it relies on. An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover that.
- **Push back:**
  - A Completion deliverable (or CP) of proof of cleared payment and a **confirmatory IP assignment deed** from Ironquay. Payment can be funded from price if needed.
  - Broaden the indemnity to all Loss from any failure to own, or any infringement claim relating to, the Ironquay deliverables, outside cap and basket, with an extended time limit.
  - IP warranties should be standalone, not "settled under the general regime."

**14. Data export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006; DL 6)**
- **Facts:** The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Its own DL says scope, access and notifiability are unknown. About 1,240 records of personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity) were sent to an unintended external address.
- **Risk:** Under the Privacy Act's Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days. It is unclear whether that happened. The Seller has not said whether the OAIC and affected individuals were notified. Penalties and regulator attention in this area have increased.
- **Push back:**
  - Obtain before signing or Completion: the incident timeline, the NDB assessment, any forensic or legal advice, recall or deletion confirmation from the recipient, and any OAIC correspondence.
  - A pre-Completion covenant for the Seller to complete the assessment and any required notifications in consultation with the Buyer.
  - A **specific indemnity** covering notification and remediation costs, third-party claims, and regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable. It should sit outside cap and basket, and disclosure should not qualify it.
  - Warranties on privacy compliance and that there are no other incidents.

**15. Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011; DL 8), 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k**
- **Problem:** The Seller calls them "ordinary course," but the DL itself says this is not established and that the three are related and should be read together. Each is individually above the de minimis, but together they may be a single commitment split up.
- **Push back:**
  - Obtain the contracts and the budget. Establish whether the renewals are terminable, prepaid or accrued, whether they fell within the conduct-of-business restrictions, and whether Sandbar is related to the Seller.
  - If they are not in the budget or ordinary course, treat them as debt-like, reduce price, or require termination before Completion.
  - Ensure aggregation of related claims.

**16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- Lower priority. The DL's careful phrasing ("does not describe it as a requirement…") is not a representation that no consent is needed.
- Have our counsel review both provisions independently for change-of-control or deemed-assignment triggers.
- Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable.
- Seek a warranty that no third-party consent is required for the transaction other than those listed.

**17. DL 1.4 (no admission) and DL 11 (Buyer must evaluate)**
- These are acceptable as general drafting only if the Disclosure Letter has no general-disclosure effect.
- Make clear in the SPA that the Disclosure Letter cannot expand Seller protections beyond what the SPA permits.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Process | [STANDARD] items "FINAL" | Reject categorisation; all points open; confirm internally whether anything was agreed |
| 2 | Disclosure | General data room and registers | Specific, fair disclosure only; nothing qualifies fundamentals, tax or indemnities |
| 3 | Buyer knowledge | Excludes known or discoverable matters | Delete; express pro-sandbagging clause |
| 4 | Scope of limitations | All Claims of any nature | Warranty Claims only; carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, indemnities, leakage, covenants |
| 5 | Title / capacity | Same as general | 100% cap, 6–7 years, no thresholds; independent ASIC/PPSR verification |
| 6 | Tax | General regime | Tax indemnity/deed, 100% cap, 5–7 years |
| 7 | Cap | 20% | Acceptable for general warranties only (or consider W&I) |
| 8 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | AUD 10k / about AUD 120k tipping; related-claim aggregation |
| 9 | Time limit | 18 months | 24 months for general warranties |
| 10 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; consent letter suffices | Buyer CP: unconditional consent plus 11.3 satisfied; all reasonable endeavours; long-stop; consider revenue-protection indemnity |
| 11 | Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | Payout letter; repay from price at Completion; releases and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion |
| 12 | Bonuses (AUD 420k + on-costs) | Seller's matter; not in funds flow | Deduct as Transaction Costs incl. on-costs; payroll processing; indemnity |
| 13 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment evidence plus confirmatory IP assignment at Completion; broad IP indemnity |
| 14 | Data incident | Not material | Full information now; NDB compliance covenant; uncapped specific indemnity |
| 15 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Verify; treat as debt-like or price-adjust if not budgeted; aggregate |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed (implied) | Independent review; notice as deliverable; no-consents warranty |

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
1. The disclosure and knowledge regime, together with the scope of the limitations.
2. Fundamentals and tax.
3. The Riverlark and bonus price mechanics.
4. The Bluefen CP.
5. The Ironquay and data-incident indemnities.
6. The threshold mechanics.

Items 1–2 are the structural points. If we concede them, most of the protection on the specific issues falls away.

**Immediate information requests to Seller:**
- Bluefen consent status and the clause 11.3 conditions
- Riverlark payout figure and draft release
- DD-005 bonus terms and on-cost calculation
- Ironquay payment status and assignment
- DD-006 incident file and NDB assessment
- Sandbar contracts and budget
- Share certificates and any share security

I can turn this into a responsive mark-up of the relevant SPA clauses or a covering email to Seller's counsel if helpful.

**14. Data export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006; DL 6)**
- **Facts:** The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Its own DL says scope, access and notifiability are unknown. About 1,240 records of personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity) were sent to an unintended external address.
- **Risk:** Under the Privacy Act's Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days. It is unclear whether that happened. The Seller has not said whether the OAIC and affected individuals were notified. Penalties and regulator attention in this area have increased.
- **Push back:**

  - A **specific indemnity** covering notification and remediation costs, third-party claims, and regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable. It should sit outside cap and basket, and disclosure should not qualify it.
  - Warranties on privacy compliance and that there are no other incidents.

**15. Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011; DL 8), 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k**
- **Problem:** The Seller calls them "ordinary course," but the DL itself says this is not established and that the three are related and should be read together. Each is individually above the de minimis, but together they may be a single commitment split up.

**16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
